input:
A vapour-compression refrigeration unit is used to serve a cold store, and the operating conditions of the unit are defined by an evaporating temperature of 0 °C and a condensing temperature of 45 °C. In order to assess the performance of the unit, it is helpful to compare it with the best performance that could in principle be achieved between the same two temperatures, which is given by the Carnot coefficient of performance.

The Carnot coefficient of performance represents an ideal upper limit that no real refrigerator operating between 0 °C and 45 °C can exceed, and between these temperatures its value is 6.07. The installed unit, by comparison, achieves a coefficient of performance of 2.38, which corresponds to 39.2% of the Carnot value and therefore falls considerably short of the ideal figure, as would be expected for a real machine with real losses.

It should be noted, however, that the achieved figure is taken from the manufacturer's test of the unit at full load, and the performance of the unit at part load is not stated, so the extent to which the coefficient of performance changes when the unit is operated away from its full-load condition remains an open question that the available information does not resolve.
target:
A vapour-compression unit serves a cold store. The unit evaporates at 0 °C and condenses at 45 °C. State the Carnot coefficient of performance between these temperatures, and compare the performance the installed unit achieves.

The Carnot coefficient of performance is the upper limit for a refrigerator working between the same two temperatures: no machine on the same duty exceeds it, and real machines fall short of it through the losses their cycles contain: pressure drops in the circuit, heat transfer across finite temperature differences, and the losses of the compressor among them. Between 0 °C and 45 °C the Carnot coefficient of performance is 6.07.

The installed unit achieves a coefficient of performance of 2.38, which is 39.2% of the Carnot value: the unit returns well under half the cooling per unit of work that the ideal machine would return between the same temperatures. The comparison is made at the stated temperatures only; a change in either temperature changes both the Carnot limit and the achieved value, and the two do not move by the same amount.

The achieved value comes from the manufacturer's test at full load. Part-load performance is not stated, and the figure describes the unit at its tested duty only; the coefficient of performance at reduced load is not given by the test and cannot be read from the full-load value.
